newsitem.title: USA: AMR says didn't seek to block USAir.
newsitem.headline: AMR says didn't seek to block USAir.

text.p: AMR Corp's American Airlines said on Thursday that it had expected USAir Group Inc to continue with its code sharing agreement with British Airways Plc, despite a proposed alliance between American Airlines and British Air.
"American Airlines has never sought to interfere with the USAir-British Airways agreement and has not done so," the company said in a statement.

Earlier today USAir, which is 24.6 percent owned by British Airways, said it plans to end its code sharing arrangement effective March 1997, because of the proposed deal between American Airlines and British Air.
USAir previously filed suit to block the alliance.
Code-sharing is a marketing agreement in which airlines share passengers and extend their reach to destinations they do not typically serve.

American Airlines said USAir's termination of the code sharing plan "confirms our statements in court filings that USAir is not so much an 'aggrieved party' as it is a company that wishes to renege on a $400 million deal it now regrets."
American Airlines said it will seek a dismissal of USAir's lawsuit to block the alliance.
USAir was not available for comment.
